followups.problem: Direct-build mode still shows swarm counts in the Cockpit outside the header and tiles. paintNow is passed the real headline (line 685) and shows NEXT UP '1 / ${headline.ready}'. The idle branch (line 597) says '${model.total} tickets in the ledger' with model.total forced to 0. renderCockpit's stage strip (cockpit-view.js:218-219) still prints per-stage 'S1 done/total' and 'N OF M STAGES DONE'. The header 'agents' counter (line 99) uses the ledger running count while the 'running' tile is forced to 0.
followups.exploit_or_failure: On parts-request-app (directBuild, 40 ready), the header reads '—' and the ready tile reads 0, but the NOW card reads 'NEXT UP 1 / 40' and the stage strip shows done/total per stage. When the ledger has no ready or running lead, the card says '0 tickets in the ledger', which is false. The new test checks only .sub2, the tickets counter, .stack .n, the footer and the tiles, so it misses these.
followups.fix: When directBuild is set, pass headline=null and use '—' for the NOW card count. Replace the idle line with 'direct build'. Pass a flag to renderCockpit so the stage strip shows 'swarm counts hidden' instead of per-stage counts. Either hide the agents counter or label it consistently. Add asserts on .cn and .stripl to the direct-build cockpit test.

followups.problem: compareStageIds now also re-sorts the author-declared scope.stages list, which was used in declared order before. Non-S ids are sorted by plain localeCompare, so declared orders like ['mvp','beta','launch'] become ['beta','launch','mvp']. 'M2'/'M10' still sort as M10 before M2, and any S-id is forced ahead of every non-S id.
followups.exploit_or_failure: A project whose scope declares stages 'design','build','ship' now shows the stage strip and segment colours as build · design · ship. A scope that interleaves S-ids with named stages gets reordered. Before this change both kept the declared order.
followups.fix: Keep the declared scope.stages order and sort only the Object.keys(byStage) fallback, or sort scope stages only when every id matches /^S\d+$/. For non-S ids use localeCompare(b, undefined, { numeric: true }).

followups.problem: familyRootsForTicketLog adds every directory under SWARM_SCRATCH_ROOT for any main-checkout project. This is the same pre-existing scope as lastTicketFinishedAt, but it now feeds a counter that is summed across projects. doneLast24hCount de-duplicates ids only within one project. buildHiveExtras then adds the per-project values together and skips only projects that have directBuild set.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Suppose two registered main-checkout projects share one scratch root, or a direct-build project keeps its scratch worktrees there. Each project counts every scratch tickets.log, so one done transition appears N times in hive.doneLast24h. A direct-build project's scratch completions also land in a swarm project's count, so the 'directBuild excluded from doneLast24h' guarantee can fail.
followups.fix: Filter scratch candidates to this project's family: check that the worktree's git common dir or main root matches the anchor, as projectFamilyRoots/worktreeFamily do. Or reuse the boardSnapshot family set (familyRoots) that projectOverview already receives, instead of rescanning.

followups.problem: Each projectOverview/projectDetail call now runs familyRootsForTicketLog (a worktreeFamily git call plus a scratch readdir/stat) and doneTimes() for every root twice: once in lastTicketFinishedAt (line 1030) and again in doneLast24hCount. projectOverview already has the family roots.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Every board refresh doubles the git worktree probes and tickets.log parses for each project. With a large scratch root, this adds measurable latency to /api/board on a board that already reported host-load-sensitive timing.
followups.fix: Compute both values in one pass. For example, lastTicketFinishedAt could return { at, doneTimesById } (or take a precomputed map) so doneLast24hCount reuses it. Or pass the familyRoots already known to projectOverview.

followups.problem: Every board-produced project now carries a numeric doneLast24h (0 even when tickets.log is missing or unreadable), so the throughput24h fallback for the counter can no longer fire. The throughput24h chart is still built from ledger doneAt and other timestamps (line 302), so the two can disagree.
followups.exploit_or_failure: A project that records completions in ledger doneAt or history but writes no tickets.log transitions shows 'done 24h 0' while the throughput chart beside it shows bars for the same 24 hours. An unreadable log is reported as a true 0 rather than as unknown.
followups.fix: Have doneLast24hCount return null when no tickets.log was readable in any family root (keep 0 for readable-but-empty), so the fallback still works. Or drive the chart from the same tickets.log scan so the counter and the chart share one source.

followups.problem: Items dropped by the 48h blocker and superseded/cancelled filter, and by the directBuild skip (line 159), are removed silently: they are not added to `hidden` or `total`, which goes against the comment at line 234 that the cap 'is reported, not hidden'. Phone open/confirming counts (lines 246-247) and syncPhone still include direct-build and stale items.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Needs-you drops from 52 to 5 with no 'N auto-hidden' hint, so a blocker still unresolved after 48h vanishes from the board with no trace. The phone summary keeps counting the direct-build issues that the board no longer lists, so the two surfaces disagree.
followups.fix: Track an autoHidden count (stale, superseded or cancelled, and direct-build) and return it next to hidden so the board can show 'N auto-hidden'. Filter phone open/confirming records by the same directBuild set.

followups.problem: The 'drops stale blockers and superseded ticket rows' test never produces an inbox item with id T-9001. collect() returns only the three blockers, and the ledger loops emit only proposed and blocked tickets, so the superseded/cancelled branch of hideStaleNeedsYouItem is never exercised. The held ticket's since is exactly 2 days old, so the test also does not prove held items are exempt from the age filter.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Deleting the superseded/cancelled check in hideStaleNeedsYouItem, or applying the age filter to every kind, would still pass this test.
followups.fix: Have collect() return a human or decision item with id 'T-9001' (and one for a cancelled ticket) and assert both are dropped. Set ledger.updatedAt to 8 days ago and assert T-9002 (held) and an old proposed ticket still appear.

followups.problem: The direct-build Hive card test asserts doesNotMatch /50%/, but the fixture's percentDone is 57, so this assertion can never fail. Neither doneLast24hCount nor the board-data directBuild propagation has a test, although CHANGELOG says 'Tests: ... ticket-log done-24h count'. The only doneLast24h test (command-center-counts.test.mjs:208) sums stubbed numbers.
followups.exploit_or_failure: A regression that shows '57%' on a direct-build card would pass. Bugs in unique-id merging across family roots, the 24h window, the 5-minute future tolerance or the 0-on-empty behavior would go unnoticed, as would a projectOverview or projectDetail path that drops directBuild.
followups.fix: Change the assertion to /57%/ and also assert there is no em[data-tip]. Add a board-data test that writes tickets.log in two family roots (same id in both, one entry 25h old, one 4 min in the future, one 6 min in the future) and asserts the count. Assert that projectOverview and projectDetail return directBuild true for a flagged entry.

followups.problem: The paint signature leaves out p.directBuild. The Hive card signature (cc-hive-mount.js:1029) also does not include raw.directBuild.
followups.exploit_or_failure: If the flag is toggled in projects.json while a Cockpit or Hive tab stays open and nothing else in the project payload changes, the view keeps its old mode until another field changes.
followups.fix: Add p?.directBuild to the cockpit signature and p.raw?.directBuild to the Hive card signature.

summary: No blockers. The core claims check out. directBuild is propagated on projectOverview, projectDetail and buildProjectCockpit. buildProjectCard drops counts, percent, meter, asks, fails and building for direct-build projects, so snapshotTotals excludes them. buildHiveExtras filters direct-build projects out of throughput24h, the doneLast24h sum and hiveEvents. The inbox skips direct-build projects, and the 48h age filter applies only to kind 'blocker' (held and proposed items are untouched). The percent note is true: the denominator is unchanged and the 407 live total already excludes cancelled. The height media queries only apply at max-height 1000px, and the ring layer follows hiveGeometry. Follow-ups: (1) direct-build counts still appear in the Cockpit NOW card ('1 / 40'), the stage strip and the idle line; (2) the new comparator re-sorts author-declared scope stages, and non-S ids sort alphabetically; (3) the scratch-root scan in doneLast24hCount is not limited to one project's family, so the Hive sum can double-count and can count direct-build scratch work; (4) the family and ticket-log scans now run twice per project; (5) the counter's 0-on-missing-log disables the throughput fallback and can disagree with the chart; (6) auto-hidden inbox items are not reported, and phone counts are not filtered; (7) several new tests can never fail (the /50%/ assert and the superseded path), and doneLast24hCount and board-data directBuild propagation have no tests. Limits: I did not read tools/projects.mjs, so I could not confirm the registry loader passes directBuild through from projects.json to boardSnapshot. If it whitelists fields, the flag is lost before every path above, and that should be checked before relying on the live plan. I also did not read client-report.mjs (doneTimes semantics) or the Hive view-model file that derives p.counts and p.pct. Ring and card overlap was checked only against hiveGeometry, not in a browser. No tests were run (no shell).
